Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testIssue631` fails with a `TooManyEvaluationsException` when running the `RegulaFalsiSolver` on the function \(f(x) = e^x - \pi^3\) in the interval [1, 10]. The test expects the solver to converge to a root near 3.4341896575482003 but instead it runs out of evaluations.

The `RegulaFalsiSolver` extends from `BaseSecantSolver`. The constructor of `RegulaFalsiSolver()` calls the superclass constructor with the default absolute accuracy and sets the method to REGULA_FALSI. The `solve` method in `BaseSecantSolver` is overloaded and the one called from the test (with max evaluations, function, lower bound, upper bound) internally calls another overloaded `solve` method with an extra `AllowedSolution` argument. This further delegates to a parent class `solve` implementation.

The failure likely stems from the algorithmic or bracketing approach in the `RegulaFalsiSolver` or its base solver during root finding. Since the test fails with too many evaluations, the solver does not converge or properly bracket the root in a timely manner. It suggests the Regula-Falsi method implementation may have an issue handling certain function shapes or ranges, leading to inefficiency or failure to reduce the search interval effectively.

The root cause intuition is that the Regula-Falsi algorithm implementation in this solver might have problems like slow convergence or stagnation for exponential-based functions or specific intervals, which eventually triggers a max evaluation cutoff as seen in the test failure.

For a detailed pinpoint, inspecting the exact iterative update steps of `RegulaFalsiSolver.doSolve()` (likely overridden) or its parent's bracket update and convergence checks would confirm why evaluations overflow and pinpoint what update or check fails.

Next, it would be useful to inspect the `doSolve` or iterative solving logic of the `RegulaFalsiSolver` class itself or its closest solver base class related to the Regula-Falsi method implementation. This will help confirm the cause of lack of convergence leading to too many evaluations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
